predictive_observations: The strongest signal: the unlocked LP (RugCheck showed 0.0000092% locked, a 'danger' flag, and few LP providers). The 360m and 1440m exits show exit_liquidity = 0 and a -100% return, which fits liquidity being removed within about 6h. The report named 'liquidity can be removed at any time' as a structural risk.

The clone family, and how dead it looked. Six or more same-name 'TikTokus' siblings showed $0.03–$0.04 of liquidity but still carried $1–2M market caps. That is the signature of a pool drained at a frozen price. This token's outcome has the same shape: a last price of +27.5% over entry with zero liquidity. The report read the clones correctly as a serial launch-and-pull pattern.

The metadata said 'TikTok Official Token' and linked to @tiktok_us, but there was no website, no DexScreener profile and no real catalyst. That rules out an organic holder base that could make the pool durable. It bears on who controls the exit, not on the price path.
The report chose a 6h observation window. That window, rather than 1h, is what captured the liquidity event.
misleading_observations: The 'strong_fade' label suggested the price would decline. It didn't: at 6h the maximum favourable move (MFE) was +27.5% and the maximum adverse move (MAE) was only -1.28%. Price never touched -20%, and it hit the +1σ and +2σ upside barriers first. The loss came from the pool being drained, not from a fade. The call was right about direction but wrong about how the loss would happen.

The 3,766 unique buyers vs 104 unique sellers were read as a sign of an imminent dump. In practice the price kept climbing steadily for hours. Bot-heavy, one-sided buying did not predict near-term price weakness; if anything it came before a run-up that ended in the pull.

The '~80% of supply in non-pool top-10 wallets' overhang is uncertain. The GeckoTerminal top-10 figure may include the Meteora DBC and DYN2 pool accounts. No dump from these holders showed up in the price path, so this concern did not drive the outcome.
The momentum of the sibling 'Tiktok Coin' (+934%) was cited both as a sign of a wave and as competition that splits flow. Neither reading shows up in this token's outcome.
The counterargument that the pump could continue over 1h was actually correct: +7.75% net at 60m. It was right to include it, though it was given little weight.
evidence_that_should_have_changed_conclu: Nothing available at the time should have reversed the negative view. But the clone pattern (near-zero liquidity with frozen, non-zero market caps) and the unlocked single-provider LP pointed to an abrupt removal of liquidity, not a gradual fade. The thesis should have been framed as 'binary rug risk with a possibly rising price before it', and the continuation view should have been kept separate from the price-path view.

The live re-check (holders roughly doubled to 5,019, 1h volume $4.6M, price still rising) was evidence against a near-term price fade. It should have lowered confidence in a fade inside short windows, even while the rug risk stayed high.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: When a token's packet shows at least 3 same-name or same-ticker siblings created in the last 24h with liquidity under $1 but reported market caps over $500k, and the token's own LP is flagged unlocked with few providers, the pool's liquidity falls below 5% of its entry level within 6h at a much higher rate than in matched tokens without such a sibling pattern.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Solana memecoins under 2h old at detection, with liquidity over $100k. Uses only the packet's same_ticker_or_name_tokens and RugCheck LP-lock fields at decision time.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Siblings with near-zero liquidity but frozen market caps are a footprint of a serial deployer who drains the pools they seeded. An unlocked LP held by one or a few providers leaves that deployer free to repeat the pattern. The risk is a liquidity event under the deployer's control, not a function of price discovery.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: For tokens that meet the unlocked-LP / serial-clone conditions above, the pre-rug price path is not negative on average. Returns at 60m and to the maximum favourable move before the liquidity event are flat to positive. So a 'fade' view scored at 1h will underperform a 'rug-risk' view scored on whether liquidity survives.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Same universe as the first hypothesis. Compare the 60m return and MAE before any liquidity drop against a control group with locked LP.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: A deployer who plans to pull liquidity gains from supporting price and volume until the pull, because a higher pool value means a bigger extraction. Selling pressure stays suppressed until the exit, which is one discrete event.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: Extreme asymmetry between unique buyers and unique sellers (buyers/sellers over 20 in the first hour) does not predict a negative 1h return on its own. It is associated with a positive 1h drift when the LP is unlocked and controlled by one provider.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Tokens under 1h old with at least 1,000 unique buyers per GeckoTerminal. Split the sample by LP-lock status.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: One-sided flow in a pool controlled by one provider means few natural sellers and bot or retail buying against a deployer who is not yet selling. Price pressure stays upward until the deployer acts through the LP rather than by selling in the market.

structured_output.summary:
The report called 'strong_fade' with medium confidence over a 6h window. In the recorded outcome the price rose: +7.75% net at 60m, MFE +27.5% and MAE -1.3% within 6h, and it never touched -20%. Pool liquidity then went to zero before the 360m mark, which the scorer booked as a -100% return at 6h and 24h. The negative call paid off, but through a pull of the unlocked LP, not through a price fade.

The observations that actually bore on the outcome were ones the report did cite:
- The LP was unlocked and had few providers.
- Most of the same-template 'TikTokus' clones showed near-zero liquidity alongside frozen multi-million-dollar market caps, the footprint of a serial deployer draining pools.

Other points fed the fade framing and did not play out:
- The buyer/seller asymmetry was read as a dump signal, but the price kept rising for hours.
- The ~80% supply overhang rests on a top-10 figure that may include pool accounts.
- Talk of competition from sibling tokens did not show up in this token's outcome.

The report's own counterargument, that momentum could continue over 1h, was correct.

That a rug was likely could be read from the packet. When it would happen, and the price path before it, could not. So the outcome was partially knowable.

The outcome data also has a problem that limits how much this case should count. liquidity_collapse=false and min_liquidity_24h of about $376k contradict exit_liquidity=0 at 360m. There are only 179 bars, and the exit price is stale, identical at 6h and 24h. A data dropout can't be fully ruled out, and the scoring pipeline should reconcile these fields.

The main lesson: for tokens with this structure, frame the view as 'rug risk, with a possibly rising price before it', not as a directional fade.
